title: Read the swissuniversities country table for India before anything else — Standard XII alone does not admit you to HSG
duration_realistic: 30 minutes, but do it 18 months before intake
what_happens: swissuniversities publishes the binding country-by-country recognition table for all Swiss universities, currently valid for academic year 2026/27. Open the India entry and read the St. Gallen row. It does not say 'upper secondary school-leaving certificate'. It says a completed university degree of at least three years PLUS the HSG selection procedure. A CBSE All India Senior School Certificate or a CISCE Indian School Certificate on its own is therefore not an admissible qualification at HSG, no matter how strong the marks are. Every other Swiss university in the India row (Basel, Bern, Fribourg, Geneve, Lausanne, Luzern, Neuchatel, Zurich, USI) applies the same three-year-degree rule; only ETHZ and EPFL let Indian Std XII in, and then only via their own entrance examinations - and their bachelors are taught in German and French, so they are outside the English-taught Switzerland set entirely.
the_trap: Counsellors read HSG's own admission page, see 'a foreign upper secondary school leaving certificate has to be essentially equivalent to the Swiss maturity certificate', and assume a good Std XII qualifies. It does not. HSG defers to the swissuniversities table for the country-level question, and for India that table demands a university degree. Students who apply anyway lose the non-refundable CHF 250 application fee and the intake.
exact_quote: St. Gallen: University degree (at least 3 years) + HSG selection procedure

title: Work out whether your student is actually a realistic candidate for the three English-taught Swiss bachelors
what_happens: The entire English-taught bachelor set in Switzerland is three programmes, all at the University of St.Gallen: Business Administration (BWL), Economics (VWL) and International Affairs (BIA), each a 3-year, 180-ECTS B.A. HSG entered through the English track of the Assessment Year. Given the India rule in step 1, only three kinds of candidate can realistically get in. (a) An IB Diploma holder - the IB is recognised on its own merits, independent of nationality. (b) A British A-level holder - HSG names the A-level explicitly as essentially equivalent to the Swiss Matura. (c) An Indian-board student who has already completed a university degree of at least three years. A CBSE or ISC school-leaver with no other qualification is not a candidate and should be redirected to another country. Note that Indian students at international schools in India or the UAE sitting the IB or A-levels are judged on that curriculum, not on their passport.
the_trap: Treating 'Switzerland' as an open destination for the CBSE/ISC mainstream. For the English-taught route it is effectively an IB/A-level destination. The other Swiss universities are excluded for a different reason - ETH, EPFL, UZH, Basel, Bern, Geneva and Lausanne teach their bachelors in German or French - so there is no English-taught fallback inside the country.
exact_quote: A foreign upper secondary school leaving certificate has to be essentially equivalent to the Swiss maturity certificate (such as a German Abitur or British A-level).

title: Choose the English track of the Assessment Year, and confirm the ECUS complementary examination does not apply to you
what_happens: All three majors are entered through a common first year, the Assessment Year in Economic Sciences, which can be taken entirely in English or entirely in German. The English track offers Economics and International Affairs; Law and Computer Science Assessment Years are German-only. The track language you pick at application is binding, because the HSG selection procedure must be sat in that same language. No English certificate is required at application - HSG asks only that you can cope, recommending C1 CEFR at the start of studies, and offers a free Oxford English Placement Test for the English track. Some countries' certificates trigger the Complementary Examination ECUS, which forces German B2 regardless of track; India's St. Gallen row does not, so an eligible Indian candidate is not pushed into German.
the_trap: Picking the German track by default, or from the assumption that a Swiss university must be taught in German - which then forces the aptitude test and video interview to be sat in German. The track choice is made at application and quietly determines the language of the exam that decides admission.
exact_quote: You must complete the HSG selection procedure in the language that you specified as your language of instruction for the first year of your programme (Assessment Year).

title: Open the HSG online application inside the 1 October - 30 April window and pay the non-refundable application fee
duration_realistic: 2-3 hours to complete; the window itself is 7 months
what_happens: There is one intake a year and it starts in the autumn semester. The application period runs 1 October to 30 April; for autumn 2027 entry that is 1 October 2026 to 30 April 2027. You apply through the HSG online application tool and pay an application and processing fee of CHF 250, rising to CHF 268 from autumn semester 2026 onward. The fee is explicitly non-refundable, including if you withdraw or are rejected. After submission you hear from the Admissions Office within four weeks at the latest, and all correspondence arrives in two places: the status page of your Online Application account and a separate electronic Compass Mailbox.
the_trap: Two traps. First, some HSG programme factsheets state a '1 February to 30 April' window, which contradicts the admission page's 1 October to 30 April; treat the admission page as authoritative but apply early, because the early date drives selection-procedure scheduling (step 6). Second, students ignore the Compass Mailbox because it is separate from the status page, and miss the letter that tells them how to register for the selection procedure.
exact_quote: The degree programme starts in the autumn semester. Please apply online. The application fee is CHF 250. Application period: 1 October - 30 April

title: Upload the document set - and get translations right, not attestations
what_happens: Everything is uploaded electronically as PDFs: digital passport photo, signed Enrolment Agreement, passport or ID, a CV on the HSG template, your foreign upper secondary school-leaving certificate, certificates from the last three school years, and predicted grades if you are an IB, A-level or AP candidate. If you do not yet hold the leaving certificate you upload it later, but no later than the start of the course. Documents issued in German, French, Italian or English are accepted as they are; anything else needs a certified translation into German or English. HSG is explicit that you must not post original documents.
the_trap: Indian applicants routinely send notarised or 'TRUE COPY' attested sets because that is the domestic habit. HSG does not ask for attestation, only for legible PDFs and certified translations where the language requires it - and later, at the visa stage, the Swiss Embassy in New Delhi actively rejects academic copies bearing such stamps (step 11). Attesting everything up front creates a document set that fails the visa checklist.
exact_quote: If any of the documents are not issued in German, French, Italian or English, you must also submit a certified translation of the document in German or English.

title: Get recognised, then register for the HSG selection procedure - the 10 January cut-off decides your whole timeline
duration_realistic: Registration takes minutes; the consequence lasts 5 months
what_happens: Once your full application is in and HSG has recognised your prior qualification, a registration letter appears in your Compass Mailbox with instructions for booking the selection procedure. There are exactly two sittings per year and you may choose only one: calendar week 7 (February) or calendar week 23 (June). The gate is hard: submit your complete application by 10 January and you may register by 31 January for the February sitting; submit later and only the June date remains. For the 2026 cycle HSG published the online aptitude test on Tuesday 10 February 2026 and the video interview on Thursday 12 February 2026 for week 7, and Tuesday 2 June 2026 plus Thursday 4 June 2026 for week 23. As of 14 September 2026 the page still shows these 2026 dates; the 2027 equivalents were not yet published, so confirm them before advising a student.
the_trap: This is the single most expensive scheduling mistake in the Swiss chain. A student who applies in March gets the June sitting, and the video-interview result can take up to 21 days, pushing the admission letter to late June or early July. The cantonal migration file cannot open without that letter, and the embassy itself quotes 8-12 weeks for the decision - which lands after StartWeek in calendar week 37. Applying by 10 January and taking the February sitting is what makes the visa arithmetic work at all.
exact_quote: If you submit your complete application by January 10, you can register by January 31 for the selection procedure in February. For later applications, only the date in June is available.

title: Sit the two-stage selection procedure: 70-minute online aptitude test, then a recorded video interview
duration_realistic: Two fixed appointments in the same week, plus prep
what_happens: Stage one is a computer-based aptitude test taken at home on a notebook or desktop PC with a working camera, microphone and sound - smartphones and tablets are barred. It runs 70 minutes across two sections, 'quantitative problem-solving' and 'diagram interpretation and tables'; a simple pocket calculator is allowed, dictionaries are not. About ten days beforehand the test provider emails you directly. Stage two, by invitation based on the test result, is a video interview of four to six pre-recorded questions on motivation and interests, roughly ten minutes, recorded via webcam. Both stages must be completed in the language you chose for the Assessment Year. Places for foreign applicants are capped by law, and school grades do not count: only the selection-procedure results decide.
the_trap: Students prepare like it is a syllabus exam. It is an aptitude test, and the free official practice test is the only meaningful preparation. The harder trap is that the test can only be taken once per academic year - a failed attempt means waiting a full year, not a retry in June. Also check the CET timing against Indian time zones in advance: a 2 p.m. CET start is 6.30 p.m. IST.
exact_quote: The online test is divided into two sections: "quantitative problem-solving" and "diagram interpretation and tables". The test lasts 70 minutes.

title: Receive the Letter of Admission in the Compass Mailbox
duration_realistic: Status updates by noon Thursday after the test; final decision up to 21 days after the interview
what_happens: By midday on the Thursday after the online test your Online Application status changes to 'Conditionally accepted', 'Declined', or 'Video interview'. If you go through to the interview, the status is updated no later than 21 days after it. A few days after the final decision the Letter of Admission or Letter of Rejection lands in your Compass Mailbox. Admission is conditional until you supply the outstanding school-leaving certificate; once you do, HSG confirms unconditional admission with your matriculation number. That admission letter is the document the cantonal migration authority and the Swiss Embassy both need, so nothing downstream can start before it exists.
the_trap: Counting on the 'conditionally accepted' status as sufficient for the visa file. The Embassy checklist asks for an acceptance, confirmation or registration letter from the university - and the cantonal office wants an Immatrikulationsbestaetigung, a matriculation confirmation. Students waiting on May board results for a conditional offer can find the unconditional paperwork arrives too late for an 8-12 week visa decision.
exact_quote: A view days after the final decision, you will receive the Letter of Admission or the Letter of Rejection in your electronic mailbox (Compass Mailbox).

title: Budget the real number: tuition for foreign nationals plus HSG's own cost-of-living figure
duration_realistic: Settle before the visa file is built
what_happens: HSG charges by nationality, not by EU/non-EU. The currently applicable Bachelor rate for foreign nationals is CHF 3,129 per semester; from autumn semester 2026 it rises to CHF 3,343.50 per semester, roughly CHF 6,258 to CHF 6,687 a year. Swiss nationals pay CHF 1,229 rising to CHF 1,310.50. On living costs HSG publishes CHF 2,175 per month for Bachelor students (CHF 13,050 a semester), sourced from the Federal Statistical Office 2024 student survey, and tells applicants outright to expect total costs of CHF 25,000 to CHF 30,000 a year.
the_trap: Older agency sheets and even earlier versions of this dataset quote roughly CHF 1,456 a year for HSG tuition - that is the Swiss-national order of magnitude, not the foreign-national rate, and it understates the real figure by more than four times. Quoting it to a family sets up a funding shortfall that surfaces at the cantonal proof-of-funds stage, when it is too late to fix.
exact_quote: We recommend that you expect total costs of between CHF 25,000 and CHF 30,000 per year.

title: Build proof of funds to the Canton of St.Gallen's published standard - not to the CHF 21,000 figure circulating online
what_happens: The Migrationsamt of the Canton of St.Gallen publishes its own leaflet for third-country students and doctoral candidates. It accepts two forms of evidence: bank documents, or a declaration of guarantee from a solvent person resident in Switzerland, who must attach their last tax bill and a debt-collection register extract. If the stay is self-financed, the canton wants a confirmation from a financial institution domiciled in Switzerland - a bank or the Post - showing sufficient funds, and it names a minimum of CHF 2,000 per month. Over a twelve-month year that is CHF 24,000, and HSG's own budget guidance of CHF 25,000-30,000 sits above it. Sources disagree here and you should know it: the widely repeated 'CHF 21,000 per year' is not a figure St.Gallen publishes, and no SEM page states it either; plan against the cantonal CHF 2,000 per month and HSG's CHF 25,000-30,000, not against CHF 21,000.
the_trap: Assembling only Indian bank statements. The canton's wording for a self-financed stay asks for a confirmation from a Swiss-domiciled bank or Post, which takes weeks to arrange from India, and the leaflet also states that every document not written in German must be translated - a separate cost and delay from the English translations HSG accepts. Families who budget to CHF 21,000 arrive under the cantonal threshold.
exact_quote: Bestaetigung eines in der Schweiz domizilierten Finanzunternehmens (Bank oder Post), aus der ersichtlich ist, dass genuegend finanzielle Mittel fuer diesen Zweck vorhanden sind (mindestens Fr. 2'000.00 pro Monat)

title: Take IELTS or TOEFL anyway - HSG does not require it, but the Swiss Embassy in New Delhi does
what_happens: HSG states plainly that you do not need to submit proof of language proficiency when you apply. The Swiss Embassy to India and Bhutan takes the opposite position in its own D-visa student checklist, where under 'Proof of academic degrees' it states that an English language certificate such as TOEFL or IELTS is mandatory, with German, French or Italian certificates supplied if available. The same section demands original plus two sets of coloured copies of the Secondary School Examination, Senior Secondary School Certificate Examination and University Certificate, and expressly forbids stamps such as 'TRUE COPY' or 'NOTARY' on them.
the_trap: The highest-value contradiction in the whole Swiss chain, and it is invisible if you only read the university's pages. A student follows HSG's guidance, skips IELTS, is admitted, then discovers at the visa counter that the embassy file is incomplete - and the test, booking and result cycle takes weeks the 8-12 week visa clock does not have. Book IELTS or TOEFL the moment the student commits to Switzerland. The second half of the trap is the attestation rule: Indian families attest academic copies by reflex, and attested copies are refused.
exact_quote: English language certificate such as TOEFL or IELTS is mandatory. German, French or Italian language certificates if available.

title: Lodge the national D visa in person at the Swiss Embassy in New Delhi - in triplicate, and free of charge for students
duration_realistic: 1 appointment, plus 2-4 weeks to get the slot in peak season
what_happens: A stay over 90 days needs a national D visa, not a Schengen C visa. The application must be submitted personally at the Visa Section, Embassy of Switzerland, Chandragupta Marg, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi 110021, with the appointment booked through the VFS Global Switzerland-India scheduling page. Because the decision is made in Switzerland, the embassy asks for three completed and signed application forms plus one original and two copy sets of every document, unstapled and in the exact order listed. The file includes a valid passport issued within the last 10 years with at least three months' validity beyond the scheduled return and two blank pages, four passport photographs on white background no older than six months, a signed personal cover letter covering why Switzerland, post-study plans and a confirmation that the student will leave after completing studies, a CV, the HSG acceptance letter with proof of fee payment, the academic set including IELTS or TOEFL, and the financial file. That financial file wants a sponsor's written undertaking with passport copies, a clear explanation of where the money comes from (loan with bank letter, family wealth, or salary), the sponsor's ITR-V for the last two assessment years, and three months of bank statements in A4 with the bank's stamp and signature. Notably, the visa fee for the student category is free of charge; the EUR 90 rate applies only to special cases such as post-doctoral applications.
the_trap: Handing in a single set, or a stapled one, or letting the cover letter omit the explicit undertaking to leave Switzerland after the studies. All three get the file bounced at the counter, and the next appointment can be weeks away in the April-July peak. Note also that the checklist HSG-bound students need is the one whose filename says 'fee 90.00' even though the student fee inside it is nil - do not let the filename talk a family into paying.
exact_quote: Application for a student visa has to be submitted personally at the Visa Section, Embassy of Switzerland, Chandragupta Marg, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi - 110 021.

title: Understand the two-authority structure - the embassy takes the file, the Canton of St.Gallen decides
duration_realistic: 8-12 weeks end to end, and the student must wait outside Switzerland
what_happens: Switzerland splits the decision from the counter. The Swiss representation abroad receives and forwards the application, but the authorisation belongs to the migration office of the canton where the university sits - for HSG that is the Migrationsamt of the Canton of St.Gallen, Oberer Graben 38, 9001 St.Gallen. The embassy is only permitted to issue the entry visa once a positive cantonal decision has come back, and states the total processing time is approximately 8-12 weeks, varying by canton and file. SEM's own guidance is looser still: applications for a category D visa are processed by the cantons and as a rule one to several months must be expected. The canton adds two binding instructions of its own: the application must be filed at least two months before the intended start of training, and the authorisation procedure must be awaited abroad. The cantonal form is the Gesuch Auslaenderbewilligung A1, and the canton may instruct the embassy to request further documents mid-process.
the_trap: Entering Switzerland on a Schengen tourist visa to 'wait there' or to attend StartWeek while the D file is pending. The canton's leaflet forbids it in one line - the permit procedure is to be awaited abroad - and neither a personal application from inside Switzerland nor an application by a third party resident in Switzerland is possible. The second trap is arithmetic: a June selection sitting plus a late-June admission letter plus 8-12 weeks lands in September, past StartWeek in calendar week 37. The canton's own two-month minimum is a floor, not a realistic plan.
exact_quote: The total processing time is approximately 8-12 weeks. This time is an approximation only and may vary considerably depending on the canton responsible and the elements of the application.

title: Collect the D visa and travel - and know what the 2025 Entry/Exit System does and does not change for you
duration_realistic: A few days after the positive cantonal decision reaches the embassy
what_happens: Once the canton approves, the embassy issues the national D visa in the passport and the student may travel. Separately, the Schengen area switched on the Entry/Exit System from 12 October 2025, replacing passport stamping with biometric registration of facial image and fingerprints; Switzerland started at Basel and Geneva Airports on 12 October 2025, added Zurich Airport on 17 November 2025, and rolled out smaller airports such as Lugano, Duebendorf and Bern-Belp between mid-November 2025 and the end of March 2026. EES is a short-stay system: it targets third-country nationals travelling for up to 90 days and calculates their permitted stay. The Federal Council states that for third-country nationals holding a valid residence document nothing changes, so a student who is already a permit holder is outside the short-stay counting regime - but expect biometric enrolment and slower border queues during the rollout, especially on a first entry.
the_trap: EU/EEA and EFTA nationals skip this whole visa chain - they need no visa, only a valid passport or ID card, and regularise their stay through the cantonal registration in step 15. For everyone else, the practical EES risk is not legal but logistical: families travelling out with the student on short-stay Schengen visas are inside the 90-day regime and now have their entries and exits counted automatically, which matters if parents plan repeat visits across the academic year.
exact_quote: For Swiss nationals and nationals from EU/EFTA states as well as third-country nationals who have a valid residence document such as a residence permit or permanent residence permit in a Schengen state, nothing will change.

title: Register in person at the Einwohneramt within 14 days - the D visa is an entry document, the B permit comes later
duration_realistic: Register within 14 days; the permit card follows in several weeks
what_happens: The national D visa only gets you into the country. The residence permit itself is issued by the canton after you arrive. Within 14 days of moving in you must register personally at the residents' registration office of your municipality - for the city of St.Gallen that is the Einwohneramt, City of St.Gallen, Poststrasse 28, Rathaus, 9001 St.Gallen - bringing your passport and travel documents, and paying a registration fee. The municipality forwards the file; once the Migrationsamt approves, it issues the foreign national's identity card and invites you to the Ausweisstelle for a biometric appointment, where you present a valid travel document. HSG's own guidance to incoming students states the same 14-day rule.
the_trap: Treating the visa sticker as the permit and skipping registration during the busy first fortnight, which collides with StartWeek and finding housing. The 14 days run from the date you move in, not from your first lecture. A second, quieter trap: registration in St.Gallen presumes deregistration from your previous place of residence, and the permit card takes weeks to arrive - so do not plan travel out of Switzerland, including a first trip home, until the card is in hand.
exact_quote: You must register any relocation, move in and around the city, or change of place of residence within 14 days

title: Settle health insurance within three months - either buy Swiss KVG cover or actively apply for exemption
duration_realistic: Do it in the first month; the legal deadline is 3 months
what_happens: Swiss health insurance is compulsory under the Federal Health Insurance Act (KVG, SR 832.10) for anyone taking up residence, and cover must be taken out at the latest three months after taking up residence in Switzerland. Sign up inside that window and cover applies retroactively from the date of residence; sign up late and cover only starts from the date of enrolment, leaving a gap you pay for yourself. Students are one of the categories that can be exempted instead. The exemption is not automatic - you apply to the cantonal authority, which in practice is the Kontrollstelle fuer Krankenversicherung of your St.Gallen municipality (in the city: Rathaus, 9001 St.Gallen, kvg@stadt.sg.ch, +41 71 224 53 57), using their official form 'Gesuch um Befreiung - Meldeformular fuer Studierende'. Your foreign insurer must confirm unconditionally on that form that your cover is equivalent to KVG; the office states that confirmations in any other form are not accepted. An exemption runs for a maximum of three years and can be extended on request by up to three more - which covers a three-year Bachelor.
the_trap: Assuming an Indian travel or student policy automatically counts. Two things break it: the cover has to be equivalent to Swiss statutory cover including treatment in Switzerland, and the insurer has to sign the canton's own form without conditions - most Indian policies will not. Students also miss that the exemption is a request with a deadline attached to the three-month insurance window, not a passive status. If it is refused at month four, Swiss premiums of roughly CHF 190 a month in HSG's own budget apply, backdated or not, and the exemption must be renewed before it lapses at three years.
exact_quote: Versicherungsbestaetigungen in anderer Form werden nicht akzeptiert

title: Work rights: nothing for the first six months, then a maximum of 15 hours a week with a permit application per job
duration_realistic: First eligible from month 7 of studies
what_happens: Third-country students in St.Gallen holding an education residence permit may work a maximum of 15 hours a week during the semester, and full time during semester breaks if they apply and the institution consents in writing. The restriction that catches everyone is the waiting period: for students at a university or university of applied sciences, secondary employment may be authorised at the earliest six months after the start of studies. The exception is narrow - a student with a foreign Bachelor's degree enrolling in a Master's in the same or a similar field may start at the university's own specialist institute without the six-month wait, which does not help a first-year Bachelor student. Before starting any job you must file a Stellenantrittsgesuch with the Migrationsamt, which also checks that pay and conditions match local, occupational and sector norms, and a change of job needs a fresh authorisation. Work in your own scientific specialist field may be authorised separately. After graduating from a Swiss university you get six months to find qualified employment under Art. 21(3) of the Foreign Nationals Act; that six-month job-search permit is not extendable.
the_trap: Building the funding plan around part-time earnings from day one. For an autumn-start Bachelor the first legal working day is around March of the following year, so the entire first two semesters must be funded from the proof-of-funds pot. HSG's own incoming-student fact sheet is blunter still, warning that a student visa does not entitle you to work and that students without EU/EFTA nationality are highly unlikely to receive a work permit - so treat any earnings as upside, never as budget. Working over 15 hours without converting to an employment permit puts the residence permit itself at risk.
exact_quote: Bei Studierenden, die an einer Hochschule oder Fachhochschule in der Schweiz eine Aus- oder Weiterbildung absolvieren, kann die Aufnahme einer Nebenerwerbstaetigkeit fruehestens nach 6 Monaten bewilligt werden.

title: Enrol for the semester and attend StartWeek in calendar week 37
duration_realistic: StartWeek is 1 week; semester begins the following week
what_happens: The final HSG steps run in parallel with the immigration ones: set up your user account, complete semester enrolment and pay the semester invoice at the foreign-national rate, then attend StartWeek, which is mandatory and falls in calendar week 37, with teaching starting in calendar week 38. Practically this means the student must be physically in St.Gallen in mid-September, with housing found and the Einwohneramt registration under way inside the same fortnight. The cantonal file (step 13) must therefore have been decided weeks before, because the authorisation procedure has to be awaited abroad.
the_trap: Everything converges on one week. StartWeek attendance, the 14-day registration clock, the housing search and the three-month insurance window all begin within days of each other, while the visa decision that enables them all takes 8-12 weeks upstream. Counting backwards from calendar week 37: the D visa file should be lodged in New Delhi by roughly mid-June at the latest, which only works if the student sat the February selection procedure - which in turn only works if the complete HSG application was in by 10 January.
exact_quote: Das Gesuch ist in jedem Fall mindestens 2 Monate vor dem Beginn der beabsichtigten Ausbildung einzureichen. Das Bewilligungsverfahren ist im Ausland abzuwarten.
